# CHANGELOG: TAOM (Tales From the Age of Men)

> **Generated at each release; do not edit by hand.** `/release` runs
> `python tools/changelog_from_commits.py --version vX.Y.Z --write`, which adds one section per
> release from the subjects and bodies of every commit since the previous release tag. The commit
> body is the changelog entry, so write it for a reader of the release note. Between releases,
> `git log <last tag>..HEAD` is what changed.
>
> **Archive:** the hand-written entries from 2026-07-01 up to the switch to generation are in
> [`docs/changelog-archive/CHANGELOG-2026-H2-handwritten.md`](docs/changelog-archive/CHANGELOG-2026-H2-handwritten.md);
> older ones are in [`docs/changelog-archive/CHANGELOG-2026-H1.md`](docs/changelog-archive/CHANGELOG-2026-H1.md).

#### feat(realms): v2.0.38 - Ruling houses keep their own banner

`979db2d1`

A ruling house keeps its own banner, apart from its realm's. The house's
parties on the map, the encyclopedia and the banner editor show the house
banner; its settlements, the clan screen, battles and the kingdom pages
show the realm banner.

A title can carry a banner in realms_titles.xml; a realm flies the banner
of its ruler's primary title. Lindon, Gondor and Mordor's kingdom titles
carry their kingdom's starting banner. A ruler with several titles of
their highest rank can make one primary on its title page; style, party
name and realm banner follow it, inheritance laws do not.

#### feat(story-missions): v2.0.38 - The Hornburg window offers its battle

`c700fac3`

The War Chronicle's "Battle of the Hornburg" used to end with "No
assault comes to Helm's Deep" whenever no AI army besieged Helm's Deep
inside its 20 day window, because the chronicle starts no battle of its
own. Now the window offers the player the Helm's Deep defence (#1105,
slice 4).

When the window opens and the map is free, a popup offers "Ride to
Helm's Deep" or "Not now". Riding there opens a menu with "Defend the
walls" and "Let fate decide".

- A won defence resolves the event Held at once.
- A lost defence, or a retreat after the battle starts, gives Helm's
  Deep to Isengard with an empty garrison and no militia, and the event
  resolves Fell.
- "Let fate decide" is saved. If no siege comes before the close day,
  the window ends Held by fate ("at dawn the Hornburg still stands"):
  it pays the Held effects, including +100 Free momentum, and The Last
  March of the Ents can follow.
- "Not now" and Escape only snooze the offer to the next campaign day.
- A real Isengard or Dunland siege still decides first: no offer while
  one is under way, after one, or once the defender has lost the
  fortress.

No offer appears in co-op, while enlisted, as a prisoner, in a map
event, after War Ended, to a player whose kingdom is one of the
attackers, or with the new War Chronicle setting "Offer Story Missions"
off. The window then resolves by the map and by fate as before.

The battle result is applied when the result menu opens, so a save on
that menu keeps it. Old saves load: the new saved decline flag is
optional.

Review: /deep-review tier 1 (Codex, Lenses 2, 5 and 7) found no HIGH;
8 MEDIUM and 11 LOW were fixed with tests. RCA:
docs/reviews/rca-story-missions-slice4-2026-11-13.md

Not-tested: the in-game rows in tools/ingame_checks/1105.toml (win,
loss, decline, snooze, save on the result menu). The 15 new text keys
await the language pass, so the language-row test is red for them.

#### feat(dialogue): v2.0.38 - Encounter lines by people and player's side

`913cba78`

Lords, caravans, villagers, bandits and hideout chiefs now speak in
their own people's voice, and the words change with who the player is
to them. 681 new English lines replace the base game's Calradian text
in these encounters.

Speakers: 9 peoples (Men of the West, Rohirrim, Northmen, Dunlendings,
Southrons, Easterlings, Elves, Dwarves, Orcs and Uruks) and 10 bandit
clans (the 8 Bandit Voices clans plus Feral Orcs and looters).
The player's place: liege, ally, rival, foe or kin for lords;
kin, friend or foe for caravans and villagers; kin, same side or foe
for bandits. Worked out from the player's realm, side
(execution/alignment.json) and people (culture group, race family).

How:
- Lord lines are tag-scored variants of vanilla ids
  (str_context_line, str_surrender_demand_hero, str_surrender_offer,
  str_prisoner_released, hero_leave) in
  taom_encounter_lord_strings.xml, with 15 new conversation tags
  (taom_speaker_<group>, taom_player_<bucket>, taom_alt_line).
- Caravan and villager greetings and surrender lines, the hideout
  chief's challenge and bandit robbery sets come from a keyed table,
  taom_encounter_strings.xml, through Patch149_EncounterLines
  (4 postfixes). A missing row leaves the base game's line.
- Bandit Voices: the attack greeting now picks the clan line 25%,
  a people-and-side line 50%, the base game 25%. Robberies use the
  new sets half the time for the 8 clans, 80% for Feral Orcs and
  looters.
- Data: encounter_lines/encounter_groups.json (culture to group,
  race to family, bandit clan side), with a coverage test.
- MCM: World/Encounter Lines, on by default.

Every line is gender-neutral, never names the listener's people, has
no placeholder and no Calradian names. A separate lore review checked
all 681 lines; its fixes are in.

Localization: 681 new English keys (taom_enc_*) in two new files,
listed in tools/_loc_sources.py. The language files and the two
language_data.xml entries are left for the translation pass, so
EveryLanguage_DeclaresARowForEveryEnglishKey and
LanguageManifests_EveryEnglishSource_HasExactlyOneLanguageFile are
red until then.

No GitHub issue: the owner asked for this work directly.

Not-tested: in game. Tag scoring, the sentence-text seam, the
caravan and villager first-meeting reads and the hideout clan id are
covered by unit and binding tests only.
Save-compat: no save data.

#### feat(long-defeat): v2.0.38 - Groundwork for upgrading bought troops

`313400cf`

Players asked to upgrade the soldiers they already have in the shop,
from militia up each step of the troop line (#1161). This lands the
rules and the engine step; nothing changes in play yet, because no
fortress's shop.json lists an upgrade step.

- shop.json can list `upgrades` rows: from, to, price per soldier and a
  name. A bad row, a repeated step or a step that would close a loop
  is skipped with one warning, so every line ends.
- Between waves the run knows how many soldiers of each troop stand.
  A buy takes every unsold one the gold pays for; on the next tick each
  is faded and the new troop spawns at his place, facing and formation
  with the same health share. Soldiers not replaced are refunded.
- Mounted soldiers, heroes, engine crews, tower posts, the player and
  the lord are never upgraded. A fade is a rout to the engine, which
  the run and the morale logic count as no loss.
- The bot buys an affordable upgrade after its packs and
  fortifications, the run report adds
  the `upgrades` sink, the `upgrade` purchase kind and its count, and
  a `taom.long-defeat.upgrade` check counts the soldiers replaced and
  reads their troop ids back.
- The run judge accepts the new sink; it refuses an upgrade purchase
  until its price check lands with the shop steps.

Also fixes the #1160 manifest's fixed_in to name the fix commit.

Owed in a follow-up worktree: the Rohan steps in shop.json, the shop
panel rows and their text, the judge's upgrade check, the feature doc,
/verify, /deep-review and the game proof.

Tested: dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~LongDefeat, 2,699
passed; tools.tests.test_run_long_defeat, 457 passed. The full suites,
/verify and /deep-review were skipped on the maintainer's word to land
the branch now.

Refs #1161

#### feat(hall-seats): v2.0.38 - Seat only as many lords as the hall holds

`04e328bd`

Every lord in a town or castle goes to the lord's hall, and a lord
past the free sp_notable and common spots spawns on the first usable
point of any tag, which vanilla never marks used. With 10 lords per
clan in several kingdoms, a hall could show 20 to 40 lords packed onto
one spot at the door; orc lords in their armoured civilian outfit read
as a block of soldiers.

Hall Seats (Patch148, MCM Fief Management/Hall Seats, on by default)
opens one spawn pass around MissionAgentHandler.SpawnLocationCharacters
and, in the lord's hall only, returns a null agent from
SpawnDefaultLocationCharacter for a lord with no seat. Seats are the
free sp_notable, npc_common_limited and npc_common spots less the other
characters that land on them. The player clan, the owner clan leader,
a kingdom leader, the governor, issue and quest givers, quest targets
and the lord the overlay opened the hall for always spawn; the rest
rank by owner clan, clan leader, clan tier, renown. Held-back lords
stay in the location list, so campaign state is unchanged.

#### feat(tools): v2.0.38 - Add Blender mesh gates and blender-asset skill

`0826ad31`

A mesh can now be checked in Blender before it goes to the Modding
Kit, by one tool with one verdict. Until now the checks sat inside
six tools, each for one kind of asset, and a prop modelled by hand
passed through none of them.

- tools/blender/mesh_preflight.py reads an FBX or a .blend as the
  export will write it and reports FAIL, PASS WITH NOTES or PASS.
  It fails a run for faults TAOM has met before: faces wound
  inward, a material named x.001, no UV layer, a prop with no bo_
  collision twin, unweighted vertices, more than 64 bones.
- tools/blender/qa_views.py renders six views with back faces
  culled, as the engine draws them, so a face wound the wrong way
  shows as a hole. Blender's own views draw both sides and hide it.
- The /blender-asset skill holds the rules for a live Blender MCP
  session, a table of which workflow owns which Blender task, the
  two gates, and the steps for matching a reference picture.

The idea of a routed pipeline with a checklist gate and a verdict
backed by screenshots comes from arjun988/blender-skills (MIT).
Nothing from it is installed, and its rules for other engines
(collider and LOD names, texture packing, budget tables) were not
taken. The record is
docs/reviews/adopt-blender-skills-2026-11-13.md.

Measured in Blender 5.3.0: the approved erebor_dwarf_house_01
passes with notes, and a copy with flipped walls, a .001 material
and no collision body fails on all three. The first run failed the
approved house at 0.99% of its surface (thin trim slabs with a
face right behind each), so only a share over 5% fails a run and a
smaller one sends the reader to the views.

Not run: the check inside a live Blender session, a skinned mesh
in Blender, and the routing eval for the new skill.

Refs #1153

#### feat(long-defeat): v2.0.38 - Split the defenders at each wave's start

`725725c3`

At the start of each wave the defenders of The Long Defeat now stand
in four groups instead of one. The infantry split between the wall
and the gate, and the archers between the lower wall, where the siege
towers come, and the high walls. Helm's Deep ships 70/30 for both,
wall heavy. Before, the siege AI sent every soldier on foot to the
gate until the first attack landed: it defends only the gate lanes
while no lane is active, and merges its melee formations to them.

The places come from the scene's own siege objects: the outer gate,
the wall segments on the other lanes, and the defender archer
positions below and above the wall line. A place needs a navmesh and
must lie inside the boundary. In each calm, once the garrison or a
pack has mustered, the groups are taken off AI control and ordered
with the shapes of vanilla's ready orders. They are handed back to the
AI at the first contact, when a siege lane's defense level rises
above its level at the hold. A group whose movement order the player
changed stays with the player. A pack that musters during a hold joins
the group below its share, and the soldiers already placed stay put.
The engine gives every formation back to the AI when the lord's body
falls or a new one is adopted, so the split is made again on the next
tick.

A fortress row turns this on with a split block in fortresses.json,
{"wallFoot": 0.7, "lowArchers": 0.7}, each share from 0.05 to 0.95. A
row with no block plays as before; a bad block logs one warning and
does not split.

The new check taom.long-defeat.split is written at the release. It
passes when each group holds soldiers and stands within 25 m (foot)
or 40 m (archers) of its place. A short hold, the stalemate charge, a
wave that cleared with no contact, the run's end, or a release with
no group still held is a named skip. A scene that gives no places for
a pair fails with reason=no-places, and the other pair is still split.
tools/run_long_defeat.py owes one split pass once the log shows a
calm's split and a wave cleared, and its fail message now keeps the
whole failed line (up to 400 characters) for every Long Defeat check.

Tests: DefenderSplitTests, LongDefeatSplitReaderTests,
LongDefeatSplitChecksTests (including the sanitised line against the
manifest pattern), LongDefeatDirectorSplitTests and the split cases
of test_run_long_defeat.py. Review: tier 1 deep review in two waves;
13 confirmed findings fixed, recorded in
docs/reviews/rca-long-defeat-split-2026-11-12.md. Codex did not run.

Not-tested: no game run yet. Owed in game: a --waves 2 run that shows
the four groups' places, a split pass with kept=0, whether a lane
rises early, whether the held archers climb to the wall points, and
whether the wall line's middle has a navmesh. Whether the check
should also judge height is the maintainer's call.

Refs #1128, #1079

#### feat(hero-auras): v2.0.38 - Heroes strengthen the troops around them

`5ed539e3`

Named heroes now strengthen the allied soldiers within 15 m of them,
each in his own way (#1127). Seven auras ship in
hero_auras/hero_auras.json, each tied to specific heroes by id:

- Aragorn: men near him hold their nerve, take 10% less damage and
  block better.
- Dain II Ironfoot: dwarves keep their feet and their shields up.
- Theoden: men ride harder, strike harder and keep their seats.
- Eomer: riders strike harder and are hard to unhorse.
- Elrond, Thranduil and Galadriel: elves draw faster, hit harder
  with arrows and aim truer.
- Saruman: uruks, Uruk-hai and berserkers fight on without fear.
- The Witch-king: orcs, goblins and uruks do not break.

An aura reaches every allied soldier in range, from any team on the
hero's side and the player included, but never the hero himself. It
refreshes once a second and lingers 3 seconds after a soldier leaves
the range or the hero falls. Auras run in field battles, sieges and
sally-outs, in a campaign and in Custom Battle, from the start of the
battle; not in deployment, hideouts, arenas or multiplayer. In co-op
each player gives the auras to his own troops.

The auras use the race abilities' effect channels and their model
hooks, so no new GameModel or patch is added. Where an aura and a
soldier's own race ability give the same thing, the stronger value
counts; values never add. A morale floor means the soldier cannot
rout while he carries it.

MCM, Battle Tactics/Hero Auras: Enable Hero Auras (on) and Hero Aura
Strength (0 to 2; 0 turns every aura off). The four MCM strings are
in English only for now (#763).

Not-tested: no battle has been played with this build. The in-game
check is taom.hero-auras.reached (tools/ingame_checks/1127.toml).
Review: tier 1 deep review in two waves and a convergence pass; RCA
docs/reviews/rca-hero-auras-2026-11-12.md. Codex did not run (out
of usage).

#### feat(lord-retinue): v2.0.38 - AI lords carry idle kin in party roles

`9f6b2c98`

AI lord parties now take one idle adult relative along and give that
relative a party role: scout, surgeon, engineer or quartermaster.
Vanilla never does this, so every AI party ran all four roles on the
lord's own skills.

A party takes a hero only when its clan is at its party limit, the party
rests in a settlement, and an adult member of the same clan stands in
that settlement with no party. The hero fills the empty role where the
hero most beats the lord, and is not taken when the lord is better at
every empty role. The clan leader, wounded or noncombatant heroes,
governors, notables and player-controlled heroes are never taken.

Heroes go back to the settlement when the clan drops below its party
limit (vanilla then wants them as party leaders) or when the feature is
turned off. When a party starts to disband, for example after its leader
marries away, every hero but the leader leaves it at once. Without that,
vanilla's garrison merge leaves the hero listed in the garrison with no
party.

New MCM group World/Lord Retinue: an on/off switch (on by default) and
extra heroes per party, 0 to 2 (default 1). Under co-op only the host
acts, and parties, clans and heroes of remote players are left alone.
Each extra hero costs the clan a daily wage and a party slot.

Known limitation: no in-game check has run yet. Issue #1122 carries the
triage-needs-ingame label for the marriage and party size checks.

Review: docs/reviews/rca-lord-retinue-2026-11-12.md
Refs #1122

#### feat(resources): v2.0.38 - Scale battle pay, raise emissary prices

`a629f343`

Fighting groups of 10 to 20 orcs paid 25 to 100 War Spoils a win (the
base of 50 times an enemy-to-player ratio clamped to 0.5 to 2), and an
Elite Emissary troop cost 6 to 45, so one small fight bought several
tier 9 and 10 troops early in a game.

Battle pay now follows the enemy's size alone: the resource's base
times enemy men divided by battle_reference_size (default 100),
clamped to 0.05 through 3. 15 orcs pay 2.5 of a base 50, a 100-man
battle pays 50, and 300 men or more pay 150. A party's own size no
longer changes the pay, so each co-op guest earns the same. Raid,
siege, hideout, tournament and prisoner pay are unchanged. The three
battle_* values are optional attributes on <Resource>, and an invalid
set falls back to the defaults with one warning.

The emissary's resource price is now merchant_cost times the
emissary_price_multiplier of the resource the troop's own row names:
20 for ten resources, none for War Drums, whose two creature rows are
priced by hand. A level 46 troop goes from 28 to 560 and a level 51
troop from 45 to 900. The price follows the troop, not the settlement
owner, so a defected clan cannot move it by a factor of 20. Upkeep,
upgrade and recruit costs, and the gold-only price, are unchanged.

Players see two text changes. The map-bar row reads "Per {SIZE}-man
battle", because "Per battle +50" overstated a small fight by up to 20
times, and the MCM gold-rate hint names the base cost. Both use new
keys (taom_res_tt_per_battle_ref and
taom_specres_mcm_gold_rate_hint_base) with English rows only. The 12
language rows wait for the language pass, so
LanguageFileCoverageTests lists those two keys as well.

Known effects: saves made before this change buy 20 times fewer
emissary troops with the same balance, and small fights now pay little
against elite upkeep. Watch income against upkeep in play.

pass was not run and is owed. No GitHub issue was opened for this
work.

#### feat(coop-compat): v2.0.38 - Add the TAOM.CoopCompat co-op module

`561d1b30`

TAOM.CoopCompat is a new module in the TAOM download for players who
use BannerlordCoop (#967 C3, ADR-014). It does two things:

- When a client joins a co-op campaign, it sends the server its TAOM
  build and a fingerprint of the TAOM settings that change the
  campaign. The server compares them with its own. If they differ,
  the player sees a message naming the settings groups, or a build
  warning. Nobody is kicked.
- The server sends its War of the Ring momentum to every client: on
  join, at most once a minute after a change, and once every in-game
  day. Before this, a client's War of the Ring screen stayed at the
  value from the save it joined on.

The module builds two DLLs. SubModule.xml names only
TAOM.CoopCompat.dll; every type that needs a Coop DLL to load lives in
TAOM.CoopCompat.Coop.dll beside it. The game scans every type of a
named DLL before any module starts, when Coop's own DLLs are not loaded
yet, so a Coop type there would stop the game. TypeScanGateTests keeps
it that way. The module starts at the first campaign start, so its
place in the load order against Coop and DedicatedServer.Windows does
not matter. Without Coop it writes one log line and does nothing.

TAOM.dll gains IMomentumStateStore.CaptureWarState and ApplyWarState
and TaomSettingsPages. The packager ships the module with both DLLs
and refuses any other file in its bin folders, so no Coop or server
DLL can reach a package.

The module source is mirrored in Coodsz/Coodsz-TAOM under
TAOM.CoopCompat/ (draft PR #17 there), so Coodsz's tools and this repo
work from one module.

Not tested: no co-op session yet. The first load on a client and on a
dedicated server, and a join, are owed (tools/ingame_checks/967.toml).
Owed: the Codex review (usage limit until 2026-11-14); translations of
taom_coopcompat_settings_differ and taom_coopcompat_build_mismatch,
pending the language pass.

#### feat(mission-start-guard): v2.0.38 - Name who changes a start list

`97c071c8`

A stealth hideout raid can loop the loading screen (#1028). Its log held
only "Collection was modified" and two engine frames, so nothing named
the code that changed the list. The three start helpers that Patch103
swaps into Mission.AfterStart now watch the list the engine walks around
each call (MissionBehaviors for EarlyStart and AfterStart,
MissionObjects for AfterMissionStart). When a call changes it, one
ERROR line names the list, the call, the owner's type and assembly,
both sizes and, when the list grew, the newest item. A healthy mission
start never writes it, and a mission writes at most five.

The check adds no Harmony patch. Before each call it takes a List<T>
enumerator and steps a copy afterwards. That throws exactly when the
engine's next step will, so it also sees an overwrite, a sort or an add
paired with a remove, which keep the size.

This is a diagnostic and fixes nothing. The owner named is the call
during which the list changed; it may only have called the code that
changed it. The next reproduction of the raid names the culprit, and
#1028 stays open.

Review: /deep-review tier 1 (lens 2 engine compatibility, lens 5 data
flow), RCA docs/reviews/rca-mission-list-check-2026-11-11.md, then a
re-review of the fix by lens 2 that found no defect. Codex did not run
(usage limit until 2026-11-14), so that pass is owed before merge.
Full suite: one failure outside this change,

#### feat(lost-footing): v2.0.38 - Rescue soldiers stranded off the navmesh

`e1c27ee7`

Soldiers who stand still off the walkable ground, or stuck in water,
are now moved back to where they can walk, in every field battle,
siege and sally-out (#894 phase 2). After 10 s a soldier or riderless
horse steps to the nearest good spot within 6 m at its own height
(dry land when in water). After 30 s a soldier still stuck moves to
his formation's spot, spread as vanilla spreads deployment, but only
while the player is at least 25 m from both ends of the move; that
move is tried again every 10 s while the player stays near.

Never moved: the player, fleeing men, creatures, ridden horses, men
working a ladder or machine, men on a scripted hold (a ladder queue,
a Long Defeat post, a Fords hold), and agents on a siege tower deck.
A new MCM switch, Lost Footing Rescue, is on by default; the census
switch is separate. It stands down in co-op, and the setting counts in
the co-op settings fingerprint.

Each try writes one [LostFooting] rescue line with both ends of the
move, and the summary adds rescued, freed and refused counts. Two
unattended Long Defeat runs on Helm's Deep, two waves each: before the
review fixes rescued=200 freed=167 refused=25 with 10 soldiers stuck
to the end; after them rescued=218 freed=211 refused=87 (45 on a
scripted hold) with 6 stuck, worst tick 2.90 ms. Freed means seen on
the mesh again, not proof that he walked. Nobody has watched it yet.

#### feat(tools): v2.0.38 - Gate the siege wall data of map scenes

`8a52e745`

The Long Defeat at Helm's Deep ended in a stand-off in wave 1, and a
campaign siege of Helm's Deep ran the same broken start. The base
game's siege set-up threw at the mission start, because one script
was missing in the scene file. The art pass of 2026-11-06 replaced
the right breach mesh and kept its broken_child tag, but not its
WallSegment script, and the base game reads that script on both
children of a wall with no null check. Mission Start Guard caught
the exception, so the mission went on with the walls not arranged.
The engine code is the same in v1.5.6 and v1.5.7.

The scene is fixed in the live TAOM_Map and in the testing channel
package (the two files are byte-identical). TAOM_Map is not in this
repo, so this commit holds what keeps the fault from coming back:

- tools/check_siege_wall_scripts.py reads every scene.xscene of the
  live TAOM_Map, of a folder given with --scenes, or the scene files
  named on its command line. For each wall with a side and a
  broken_child it fails when the solid_child is missing or when
  either child has no WallSegment script, and it names the scene,
  the wall and the child.
- It also fails a scene with an odd number of such walls. The set-up
  takes the walls in pairs, so a wall that lost its tag or its side
  leaves its partner to throw in the same loop.
- It runs in the tool suite against the live install, and as the
  siege-walls row of tools/data_gates.py, which hands it the scene
  files you named.
- The release process asks for it on each channel's TAOM_Map.

Checked: the gate fails on the scene as it was and passes on the
fixed one; 59 live scenes and 479 base game scenes pass. With the
script restored, the same Long Defeat match (same seed) cleared
waves 1 and 2 where it had stalled in wave 1. Not checked in game: a
full five-wave run, a campaign siege of Helm's Deep, and a breach of
either wall.

Not gated: an even wrong number of walls, the battering ram the
set-up also needs, and a wall placed as a bare prefab instance. The
patreon and public channel copies of the scene and the art mirror
were not read; a sync from the mirror brings the fault back.

Refs #1115

#### feat(realms): v2.0.37 - Feudal titles, claims and the Return of the King

`91469f71`

Realms, formerly the separate TAOM.Realms module, is now part of TAOM. Every village, castle, town and realm has a title with a holder by right, a succession law and claims. Above the counties sit 111 duchies drawn from the map's regions, the kingdoms, and the high titles of Arnor, Durin's Folk, Rhovanion and the Misty Mountains. Conquest gives a claim while the holder keeps the title; grants, gifts and sales move the title with the fief.

Gondor's throne starts vacant under Steward Denethor. A clan serving Gondor with Aragorn can restore the crown, founding the House of Telcontar in Minas Tirith. Lords are styled by what they hold on party names, in conversations and in the encyclopedia.

Claims are bought with the culture's special resource and pressed with influence. A duchy or higher can be usurped or formed once the hero's side holds most of the lands beneath it: the hero, their clan and their vassals at any depth, or for a ruler every lord of the realm. Fiefs handed to vassal clans count before their titles are pressed, and a ruler buys claims bordering any town or castle of the realm. Grants, revokes, offices (the Steward, the Marshals of the Mark, the Lieutenant of Barad-dur), weekly tribute and resentment, and grants to grown children complete the rules. Claims never start wars.

The encyclopedia gains a page for every title with its holder, seat, liege, vassals, claims, laws, chronicle and the player's actions, a Titles category, title sections on settlement, hero and kingdom pages, and a title tree. Console commands are taom.realms_*. Co-op is host only. Saves made with the old module keep their titles; disable that module. Art is placeholder and the realms_* strings are English only. The GitHub issue for this work is still to be created, and the in-game checks in docs/features/realms.md have not been run.

#### feat(story-missions): v2.0.37 - Host the Helm's Deep story mission

`97ef0231`

Slice 1 of Story Missions. A developer can open a Helm's Deep defence
from a running campaign with "taom.story_open helms_deep_defend", and
the "auto" argument lets the bot play the lord. The mission runs the
Long Defeat's wave machine on the Helm's Deep castle scene: 150 Rohan
defenders against one wave of 110 Isengard troops, all campaign troops.
The mission returns to the campaign map when the run ends. It writes
nothing to the campaign: no map event, no roster or equipment change,
no kill or capture. Players cannot reach it yet; the War Chronicle offer
comes in a later slice.

The dev menu refuses to open in co-op, while the player is enlisted,
during an encounter or a battle, and over any other open menu. Opened
inside an encounter, the mission would count as a campaign battle.

Changes to shared code, each with the old behaviour kept:
- The Long Defeat run host and mission logic take a leave action. The
  Long Defeat still ends the game; a story mission ends only its own
  mission.
- The campaign morale model holds the attackers of a hosted run, as the
  Custom Battle model already did, because the waves end only when no
  attacker stands.
- The Long Defeat gold check records a skip for a plan with no bounty
  table. A story mission has none, so a win no longer fails the check.
- Siege Dismount stands down during a story mission.

A new gate, PhotoModeEscapeMenuGateTests, fails any view list that has
the singleplayer escape menu but neither the Photo Mode view nor a view
that refuses Photo Mode. Without one, Photo Mode pauses the mission with

#### feat(war-pledge): v2.0.38 - Let Neutral realms join the War of the Ring

`65189fc4`

A Neutral realm could enter the War of the Ring only through the base
game's call to war, which starts an ordinary war that the realm can
end again. Ten kingdoms sat outside the war for the whole campaign.
Elendil proposed a lasting way in, and this is its first slice.

For players: in Full War, the side that is far behind on the war
meter (25 points or more) calls on one Neutral realm that leans its
way. Khand, Rhudaur, Umbar, Shaghana and Abanissa lean to the Shadow;
Cardolan and Dorwinion to the Free Peoples; Anduin Vale, Angaladh and
South Rhovanion lean to neither and are never called. The realm makes
peace with its new side and goes to war with every realm of the other
side, and those wars are locked like Gondor's and Mordor's. One realm
joins at a time, 30 days apart, and never a realm a player rules. A
banner and a message tell you. The switch is MCM "War of the Ring/War
Pledge", on by default, no restart; it needs Momentum Tracking on.

Limits: a pledge has no end, and turning the switch off stops new
joins only. A realm you founded is outside these wars and cannot
pledge when its culture gives it a side. A pledge breaks an alliance
or a trade agreement with the other side, charged to the pledged
realm's ruler. The player's persuasion, rumours and turning a realm
are later slices.

How: a saved pledge per kingdom is read by
AlignmentService.GetKingdomSide and
DiplomacyService.GetRelationshipTier, so the realm's side and its
Hostile tier change at the source and the three peace-block layers
lock its wars with no change of their own. The join writes the pledge,
makes peace with the realm's new side, then declares each war with the
pledged realm as the declarer. The daily step runs on the co-op
authority. Leans and the two numbers are in diplomacy/war_pledge.json.
Console: taom.print_war_pledges and taom.add_war_pledge. No Harmony
patch and no GameModel.

docs/reviews/rca-war-pledge-2026-11-10.md. No /review-codex

#### fix(troops): v2.0.38 - stop upgrades carrying weaker melee weapons

`e13bccad`

Many troops upgraded into a troop with a weaker melee weapon than the
one they had (#631). This pass walked every upgrade path and swapped
roster weapons, in every battle set, under one rule: lower tiers take
vanilla weapons and unique weapons stay with the higher tiers. No new
items were made.

Troops whose melee DPS sits 5 or more under an ancestor's went from 51
to 25 by their best battle set, and from 91 to 64 by their weakest.
No new pair was created. Rosters changed in Gondor, Cardolan, Rhudaur,
Isengard, Lothlorien, Dol Guldur, Rhun and Rohan; the Cardolan, Rhudaur
and Lothlorien generators carry the same swaps.

Three tier-1 Isengard troops gave up the one-handed Berserker sword so
its blade could be re-anchored at the champions' tier. The two-handed
Berserker sword rises from 34 to 69 DPS. The Rhudaur career kits now
start on dunland_caerdh_axe_1h_b, which the career kit rule derives
from the new rosters.

Still open under #631: class changes no swap can fix, for example the
Pavise maces and the Gundabad Chosen. Follow-ups: #1241 (restat
--culture reached Dale's blades; they were put back), #1242 (the
ladder gate scores best set only and cannot price vanilla weapons),
#1243 (engine claims in older docs).

#### fix(items): v2.0.38 - cap starter weapons at the shop's weakest one

`b2bdfdad`

A new Isengard character started with a sword that beat almost every
Isengard sword the shops sell (#1224). The starter kit generator only
lowered a starter to its weapon class's anchor, so a strong low-tier
donor made a strong starter.

A crafted starter is now capped at the melee DPS of its weakest shop
sibling: a crafted item, vanilla or Armory, of the same culture and
crafting template that a shop can sell (no tournament, practice or
unsold copies, and no lances, whose worth is the couch). Each blade
factor above that target is scaled down by the target over the donor's
DPS on that attack. The Isengard starter sword is now swing 1.48,
thrust 0.87: 29 swing damage at speed 90, the same as One-Handed
Sword II and below the Berserker sword. The cap lowered 11 starter
blades in the live Armory; every starter spear keeps thrust 1.4.

`generate_starter_kit.py --verify` now also compares the starter blade
block with the plan, so a later restat that moves a sibling blade
shows as drift instead of passing.

Tests: 86 in test_generate_starter_kit. Owed: an in-game check on a
new Isengard campaign.

#### fix(patch-notice): v2.0.38 - Name fixes that turn themselves off

`9607c9d2`

A TAOM fix that applied and then switched itself off used to go
unnoticed. Harmony counts a transpiler that finds no anchor as applied,
and the feature latches (Marshal's Word, the building UI hook, the
marriage steering, Hidden Hosts) trip long after the patch failure
notice has run. Three transpilers logged nothing at all.

Now each of 19 sites records the fix in a ledger when it turns itself
off. On the next frame TAOM writes one [SelfDisable] warning per fix to
its log. Once the campaign map or a battle is on screen, one red chat
line names every fix that is off. The id is the feature's patch
category, so a report greps straight to its heading in the patch
registry. The line waits on the map while Hide Battle UI is on, because
the game drops chat lines then; with the single-player chat box off it
is not shown and the log says so. A dedicated server logs only.

Each fix is named once per launch. Four latches outside a patch class
are not reported yet (#1223).

#### fix(staged-siege): v2.0.38 - read record times on any Windows locale

`324469a5`

StagedSiegeRecordFragment.ParseLine read "utc" through
JToken.ToString(). Json.NET has already read the ISO string as a Date
token, and ToString() formats it with the thread culture. The
invariant parse then failed on a nb-NO or de-DE Windows, every record
kept the default time, and the "newest per stage and kind wins" rule
compared equal times. A Date token is now read as a DateTime, with the
same rule as before: a time without a zone is UTC. A string token
still takes the invariant parse.

ParseLine_Valid_Record and Build_NewestPerStageAndKindWins failed on
trunk on a nb-NO PC. New test ParseLine_ThreadCulture_ReadsTheUtcTime
sets nb-NO, de-DE and en-US; it failed for nb-NO and de-DE before the
fix.

Not-tested: no game run. dotnet test --filter
FullyQualifiedName~StagedSiege: 653 passed.

#### fix(skeleton-buffer): v2.0.38 - Address cache checks the pattern too

`582ed88f`

The new address cache remembered where each byte signature was found
in the game's native code, keyed on the game file. It did not record
which pattern an address belonged to, so a later edit of a pattern
could have reused an old address as if it were still the only match.

Each remembered address now carries a hash of its pattern, and an
entry whose hash differs is searched again. Old cache files are
dropped once. A cache file that cannot be read is no longer
overwritten, so one feature cannot erase the other's entries. A file
larger than 64 KB is treated as damaged. Log lines about the cache no
longer hold the Documents path, which contains the Windows account
name. The file stamp comes from the loader's own path for the module
and no longer from a walk of every loaded module.

The feature docs now say what the cache checks and what it trusts,
that the file is per user and may sync between PCs, and that the time
saved is an estimate until a first and a second launch are compared
in game.

Review: two lenses on PR #1173 with independent verification, then a
review and a confirmation pass on these fixes.
Tests: EngineSignatureCacheTests (pattern change, failed read, size
limit, two consumers on one file), EngineSignatureCacheAdapterTests
(new, on a temp folder), AnimMemoryProbeTests,
SkeletonBufferGuardServiceTests, and one test on the installed game
file.
Not-tested: in game (the scan time of a first and a second launch).
Save-compat: no saved state changed.

#### fix(possession): v2.0.38 - Re-apply a joiner's package at the switch

`a4a41e7c`

A co-op player who joins now has their race, career and special
resource seed from character creation as soon as Coop hands them their
hero, not at the next in-game hour. Before, the re-apply waited for the
hourly tick, and a joining client's clock can stand still for minutes,
so the first battle could start with no career (BannerlordCoop #4665
logs: Coop's switch at 16:05:36, a battle at 16:17:51 with no career,
the re-apply at 16:18:05).

Coop's join hand-off calls ChangePlayerCharacterAction.Apply. Coop's
patch on Apply raises the player-character-changed event itself, and
TAOM now checks for the hand-off there. The hourly check stays as the
fallback for a co-op mod that raises no such event. The check runs
inside Coop's switch, so an error in it is logged and goes no further;
an escaped error would leave the client on Coop's loading screen. The
startup gold grant still does nothing on a Coop client: Coop lets only
the server give gold, at either time.

A new character creation now drops the picks of an earlier one in the
same game process. TAOM's Player Switcher hands the player a lord
inside character creation, before the new picks are recorded, and that
also raises the event. Without the drop, with a co-op mod enabled, a
second new campaign whose player took a lord gave that lord the first
character's race, career and resource seed.

Review: /deep-review tier 1, Agent 5 Data flow and Agent 2 Engine
compatibility, Codex at ultra; a second wave (Agents 1, 3, 4, 6) because
Codex rated the stale-picks gap HIGH (both lenses MED). Fixed before the
commit: that gap; the source pin now looks inside RegisterEvents; the
error test checks the exact message, and the log keeps the stack; the
docs cite Coop's raise site, the tick condition and where the log line
lands; the second wave trimmed comments and brought four more docs and
the #1177 issue text in line. Older, filed as #1183 (a decision owed):
with a co-op mod enabled and no session, a solo heir or a hero loaded
after a character creation can still get the package; the docs no longer
claim otherwise. RCA: docs/reviews/rca-possession-switch-2026-11-13.md,
and a lesson in lessons/campaign-mechanics.md.

Tests: PlayerPossessionSwitchTests (the three registrations inside
RegisterEvents; the handler logs and returns when the check throws),
and two service tests: a second campaign's Player Switcher before its
capture does not fire (fails with the drop removed), a join after a
completed character creation still fires.
Research: v1.5.7 ChangePlayerCharacterAction.cs:53,
Campaign.cs:977-981, CharacterCreationManager.cs:48,108-109,
CharacterCreationState.cs:62, ApplyHeirSelectionAction.cs:68; Coop
995517e60 ChangePlayerCharacterActionPatches.cs:22,30,57,65,

#### fix(diagnostics): v2.0.38 - Read the action set after the spawn ends

`cef7ec0e`

The action-set census read each agent while it was being built. In
towns, halls, villages, prisons and hideouts the game replaces the
action set after that point, so the census logged the wrong set there,
and animals and creatures spawned as monsters were not counted at all.

Each new agent is now remembered when it is created and read once on
the next mission tick, after the spawn has finished. An agent removed
before that tick is dropped. There is still no poll of every agent
every frame. A read that fails logs one warning and stops the census
for that mission, and a mission that ends before its first tick still
gets its summary.

disk when the call returns again. The notice after a write fault says
write faults, not lines. Comments, feature docs, four lessons and the
efficiency review lens now describe the logger as it is: warnings,
errors and info lines with a listed tag are written at once; other
info lines within about a third of a second.

a review and a confirmation pass on these fixes.

#### fix(hall-seats): v2.0.38 - Count each hall seat once

`1cf90d56`

Hall Seats counted the free spots of three spawn tags and added them
up. The game lists one spot under every tag it carries, and the
standard waiting spot carries two of the three tags, so most seats
were counted twice and lords still stood on one point in a full hall.

A seat is now one distinct free spot across the three tags, and one
spot seats one lord, as the game marks the whole spot used after a
spawn. A lord past the seats still falls back to one shared point
that is never marked used, which is what the feature prevents.

The rule that decides which lords always appear (the player's clan,
the owner, the ruler, the governor, a quest giver or target, and the
lord the player opens a conversation with from the town menu) is now
a plain function with one test per term. The setting is read through
the cached settings accessor. The setting hint, the feature doc and
the patch registry are corrected, and the API snapshot holds the two
new patch targets.

Known limit: a guard whose own spawn tag has no free spot left can
still take a lord's seat, so such a hall seats one lord too many.

Review: two lenses (Engine compatibility, Data flow) on PR #1158, then
a review and a confirmation pass on these fixes.

#### fix(desertion): v2.0.38 - Keep the AI lord's top volunteer slot

`3fb5a82c`

The recruit block for troops that would desert took a volunteer slot
from AI lords even when no volunteer would desert. The cap turned the
game's top value 6 into 5, and the AI recruit loop reads that value as
an exclusive bound, so a lord of a Free or Evil kingdom could never
take a notable's sixth slot, which holds the best troop.

The cap now leaves the game's value alone when no slot would desert.
With a deserter in a slot, the player can recruit up to the slot
before it, and an AI lord up to but not including it, so the AI no
longer loses a loyal slot and its trip estimate matches what it can
take.

"Only Good Rejects Evil" now spares Evil owners from desertion only
while Recruitment Alignment itself is switched on. The two setting
hints and the feature doc say what is covered: prisoners, notables'
volunteers and garrison auto-recruit. The doc lists the known limits:
tavern mercenaries are not blocked, a blocked prisoner stack still
takes conformity ticks, and a locked volunteer slot shows a relation
tooltip of 0.

Review: two lenses (Engine compatibility, Data flow) on PR #1167, then
a review and a confirmation pass on these fixes.
Tests: DesertionRecruitCapTests (rewritten: no deserter, deserter at
slot 0, 1 and 3 for the player and for the AI, never raises the
game's value) and one settings provider test for the master switch.
The player flag is passed through a thin model boundary with no test
of its own.

or is travelling waits until the lord is back on the map. That wait
can last days, and until now it showed nothing: the promised arrival
day passed, and a second messenger to that lord was refused. The
message log now says once, "Your messenger cannot find <lord> yet and
will wait until they can be reached." The line shows again after a
load, and only while the single-player chat box option is on.

One wait could never end. The engine's daily settle for fugitive and
released heroes skips a hero of the Special occupation
(HeroSpawnCampaignBehavior.OnHeroDailyTick, v1.5.7), so a messenger
to one stayed pending and blocked every later messenger to that hero.
Such a hero now counts as unreachable: the messenger is lost on
arrival, and the send refuses a released one. TAOM defines no Special
hero; SandBox gives the occupation to gang henchmen at run time, and
another mod can define one.

The new text key taom_messenger_waiting has no rows in the 12
language files yet, so the line shows in English until the next
language pass, and LanguageFileCoverageTests is red for that key
alone until then.

Two statements that set HERO_NAME on the "confused" notice are gone:
that text has no such variable in English or in any translation. The
behavior's line baseline drops from 657 to 656.

#### fix(coop): v2.0.38 - Keep the war volunteer rate off guests' fiefs

`3af437dc`

On a BannerlordCoop server, Clan.PlayerClan is the server's own clan,

checks compared the fief owner with Clan.PlayerClan. So a co-op
guest's fiefs got the volunteer rate multiplier meant for AI kingdoms,
which can raise or cut production by up to half (#1141).

before, so single player does not change. If Coop's player registry
cannot be read, no fief gets the multiplier. The server's own clan
counts as AI.

The caravan player flag is not changed. It is wrong for a guest only
when "Apply to player caravans" is off (default on); caravan-trade.md
now lists it as a known limit, with the scope of each lever.

#### fix(long-defeat): v2.0.38 - Bring destroyed siege engines back each wave

`55214715`

Players reported that a siege tower or a battering ram they destroyed
in The Long Defeat never came back, so every later wave attacked that
side without it. Now each wave start brings every destroyed ram and
tower back at the start of its path, at full strength.

The restore runs the engine's own mission reset, then sets a tower's
ladders and its waiting point back to how a fresh siege starts, puts
the engine back into its siege lane and has every attacker formation
take up its engines again, so the next wave pushes them to the wall.
A ram whose gate is already down comes back too, but has nothing to
strike until the gate is repaired.

Two new checks, engine-restore and engine-use, log whether each engine
came back at its start and whether the attackers moved it 5 m or more.
The option --break-engines N of tools/run_long_defeat.py destroys every
engine at clear N, so an unattended run can exercise the restore, and
tools/ingame_checks/1160.toml judges the lines. That run breaks the
engines between waves, so it does not cover a tower destroyed in the
middle of a wave; a played check of that case is owed.

Reviewed by Codex and three review lenses; each finding, the fix and
how it is now prevented are in
docs/reviews/rca-long-defeat-engines-2026-11-13.md.

`b9083bba`

record-session-edit.sh tells a session to read the git diff of a file
that another session edited in the last 24 hours. It did that also for
files under the user's ~/.claude folder, such as MEMORY.md, a memory
card or a plan. That folder is in no checkout, so git diff cannot show
the change. The note fired that way in a live session on a MEMORY.md
edit.

The hook still writes the ledger line for such a path, but gives no
note. The pattern is the one harness_retro.py uses to leave that folder
out of its shared-edit count, plus the Git Bash /c/ form. A repo's own
.claude folder still gets the note.

#### fix(culture): v2.0.38 - Hero agents fight for their hero's culture

`5ed0c6f5`

The player's own soldier in a battle now counts as the culture the
player picked. Before, every mission reader that took a soldier's
culture from the agent got main_hero's ModuleData culture, Khand
(culture id battania), whatever the player chose. So the player's
Culture Doctrine aggression and morale, the charge multiplier on the
player's horse, race ability kin, the player's vote for the banner a
formation carries, and formation routing all used Khand. The player's
sons copy that field at birth and read the same way.

The engine keeps a character's culture in two places. Hero.Culture is
the one character creation sets and the save keeps; the character's own
field holds the culture it got from ModuleData or its template.
CharacterObject.Culture answers with the hero's, but an agent holds its
character as a BasicCharacterObject, so a read through the agent binds
to the plain field. The new CharacterCulture.Of and IdOf read the hero's
culture first and the field otherwise, and the readers in nine files now
use them. A troop, a Custom Battle character and a hero with no culture
keep the answer they had.

On an older save, a lord whose culture TAOM's data changed after that
save now uses the culture saved with that hero. The Nine (lord_1_48_1 to
_3) moved from Dol Guldur to Mordor, so on a save from before that move
they now have Dol Guldur's never-rout doctrine. That matches the rule
that heroes keep the culture they were created with.

A new gate, CharacterCultureGateTests, scans TAOM.dll and
TAOM.Client.dll for any call that reads the plain field, and fails
unless the caller is on its list of raw readers, each with its reason.

Review: /deep-review tier 1, Agent 5 Data flow and Agent 2 Engine
compatibility, and Codex at xhigh. No runtime gap. Fixed before the
commit: the first gate was a source regex that missed a read on a
BasicCharacterObject parameter, and the no-game test step skipped it;
the doc and the helper's remarks now name the null fallback and
CharacterCreationContent.ApplyCulture. Left as is: the mount IL test
cannot tell the rider's character from the mount's (older than this
change, no issue). RCA:
docs/reviews/rca-hero-agent-culture-2026-11-13.md, and a lesson bullet
in lessons/adapters-taleworlds-api.md.

Tests: CharacterCultureTests (6: a hero by id and by object, a troop, a
hero with no culture, a Custom Battle character, no character), and
CharacterCultureGateTests (the gate, and a canary for the agent and
parameter routes; the old read put back in FormationRoutingSubscriber
fails it). MountChargeDamageBindingTests now expects IdOf.
Research: v1.5.7 BasicCharacterObject.cs:124-134,
CharacterObject.cs:264-278, CharacterCreationContent.cs:135-141,
SandBox lords.xml:11, CustomGame.OnRegisterTypes.

#### fix(patching): v2.0.38 - battle features fail apart after an update

`2d3072bf`

Smart Cavalry, Companion Tactics and Marshal's Word each patch the
game's battle order code, and all their patches were applied as one
group when the first battle starts. The game's patch library stops a
group at its first failing patch, so after a game update a single
broken patch in one of these features silently turned off the other
two as well.

Each feature now has its own group: Patch_MissionTime_SmartCavalryAI
and Patch_MissionTime_CompanionTactics are applied in that order at
the first battle, as before, and Patch_MissionTime_MarshalsWord is
applied by Marshal's Word's own module at the same moment. A broken
patch now turns off only its own feature, and the patch apply log
names which one. The order of the Smart Cavalry and Companion Tactics
patches on the same game method is unchanged.

Tests: SharedMovementOrderPostfixTests (each feature's group, the
apply order, no class left in the old group), MarshalsWordWiringTests
and MarshalThrowerWiringTests (the module's two groups), the
FeatureModules and patch registry gates, and the in-game check and
command trial patterns, which now name the Marshal's Word group.

Not-tested: in-game (a battle with all three features on)

#### fix(patching): v2.0.38 - PatchShield keeps the empty-meeting guard

`d76810a2`

PatchShield, TAOM's crash net for patches that break after a game
update, removes every unprotected owner's patches on a method once one
of them throws a missing-API exception there. TAOM's own patches all
used one owner id, which is not protected, so on the meeting method a
Refuge or Supply Lines patch that broke after an update would also have
removed the #1099 empty-meeting guard, and the crash it prevents would
come back.

The guard is now applied under its own owner id, TAOM.CrashGuards,
which PatchShield never strips. Feature patches keep the old id, so a
broken feature patch is still removed as before. The guard's own code
calls its rule inside a try/catch, so it cannot be the patch that
breaks. Other guards can join the same list in CrashGuardHarmony.

that the main id is not, and the SubModule wiring); the existing
SubModule apply gate now expects the per-category id choice.

Supply Lines patch)

`cc137ff8`

An AI ruler calling a vassal of their own title got both the King's

the call cost a quarter of the normal influence. AI armies grew larger
and lasted longer, and neither setting said so.

The liege discount now applies only the part that goes beyond the

(LiegeArmyDiscountRule, with KingsMusterService.AppliedFactor), so the

#### fix(messengers): v2.0.38 - Messengers wait instead of being lost

`e3f44a7a`

A paid messenger was lost, or came back as a mistake, in cases where
its target could be reached a little later. It now waits and is
delivered.

A messenger waits when the hero it was sent to:
- escaped a lost battle and is a fugitive,
- was just released from captivity,
- is travelling on your orders to lead a party or govern a town.
The game settles such a hero by itself, within a day or two for a
journey and usually within a few days for the other two, and the
"Messenger Arrived" choice then opens. Before, the messenger came
back with "the recipient is no longer reachable".

A messenger that arrives while you are a prisoner now waits for your
release. Before, a messenger to a hero with no party (a notable, or
a lord at home) was dropped with "they were trying to reach someone
in your own party": the game clears your party while you are held,
and the check compared the two parties directly.

A messenger to a hero who is a prisoner when it arrives is still
lost. That is the maintainer's decision for #1133.

The Send Messenger button and the dialogue line now share the
arrival's rule for the hero's state, so you can no longer pay for a
messenger that can only be lost: a disabled wanderer is refused, and
a released or travelling hero can be sent to. A fugitive is still
refused at the send, with its own reason.

While a messenger waits you see nothing, and a second messenger to
the same hero is refused as already dispatched.

For modders: IMessengerService.ClassifyArrival lost its
sharesMainHeroParty argument (HeroSnapshot.IsInPlayerParty decides),
HeroSnapshot.IsActive is gone (HeroState carries it), and the private
CanReceive is the one rule for the hero's state.

Tests: the arrival tests hold the decided rule for all eight hero
states. They replace the 256-cell comparison with the old rule, which
the refactor in #1132 used to prove that it changed nothing. The
shrink-only entry point baseline drops by the two lines the behavior
lost.

Review: /deep-review at tier 1, the data flow and engine lenses, and
a second read of the fix for the fugitive case. The record is
docs/reviews/rca-messenger-arrival-1133-2026-11-13.md. Codex did not
run (out of usage), so that pass is owed.

Known limitation: the game never settles a fugitive or released hero
of the Special occupation, so a messenger to one would wait without
end. No such hero exists in TAOM's data.

Not tested in game. The five arrival cases are checklist items 23 to
27 in docs/features/messengers.md.

Refs #1133

#### fix(harness): v2.0.38 - judge the Stop build reminder per session

`b610b35e`

The Stop hook that asks a session to build or test after a C# edit
judged the whole work tree. It counted other sessions' dirty C#, and
one shared build marker let one session's build mute another session's
reminder. The 2026-11-10 harness retro counted 32 blocks in seven days;
in 16, the C# belonged to another session or tree (#1138).

A new PostToolUse Edit and Write hook records each edited path in a
per-session ledger under .claude/logs/sessions/, and the build marker
hook also marks the session's own build. The Stop hook now reminds for
the session's own C# that is still dirty and newer than its last build.
When there is none, it reminds once for dirty C# in the work tree that
no session's ledger holds, because an edit made through Bash or
PowerShell (sed -i, git checkout --theirs) reaches no ledger. A payload
without a session id keeps the old tree-wide check. The same ledger
tells a session once when another session in the same checkout edited
the same file in the last 24 hours.

tools/harness_retro.py now measures files that two sessions edited, and
tool errors just after a compaction against just before it, so the next
retro can judge a file lease and a PostCompact hook on numbers.

#### fix(fords): v2.0.38 - Stop check 11 failing short smoke runs

`807263ca`

Check 11 failed its hits part when 20 tower missiles flew and none
hit. Tower javelins and arrows hit only 4 to 18 percent of the time in
the stored run reports, so 20 to 25 misses in a row came in about a
third of 120 second /game-run smokes (runs 20261110-154302 and
20261113-030305: 25 launched, 0 hits). Every full-length run passed.

The hits part now fails only after 400 missiles with no hit. The three
missiles of a volley share one target, so 400 missiles are about 133
independent volleys; at the lowest long-run rate on file (4.35
percent) that many misses come in about 0.3 percent of runs. Every
stored run of 300 live seconds or more launched at least 409, so a
tower that never hits still fails there. A 120 second smoke now
reports the hits part NOT_SEEN unless it sees three qualifying hits.

The deep review (data flow lens) confirmed that Launched and HitsSeen
count the same missiles, found the 20-missile rule still stated in
fords-of-war.md, and showed that a threshold of 150 counted missiles
that miss together; all three are fixed here. Not changed: a run where
only javelins or only arrows never hit reads PARTIAL, not FAIL; that
predates this fix.

Tests: two Check11 tests (399 and 400 launches, and the failing
smoke's 25), RED on the old rule; full C# suite 39,279 passed, 0
failed; canary tripped; API snapshot reproduces.

Fixes #1152

#### fix(coop): v2.0.38 - Treat co-op guests as players in four AI passes

`ab44aadb`

On a BannerlordCoop server, Hero.MainHero and Clan.PlayerClan are
the server's own hero and clan, which no human plays. Four TAOM
passes that leave "the player" alone used those two values, so they
treated every co-op guest as an AI lord (#1141):

- War Chronicle gave a guest's captive lords the extra daily escape
  roll, and gave a realm a guest rules the losing-side rally effects.
- Realms let the AI claim titles for a guest's clan, which spends the
  clan's influence and gold.
- Race fertility put a guest's marriage under the AI clan size brake
  and gave it the AI race bonus. TAOM's pregnancy model replaces the
  vanilla method without calling it, so Coop's own fix on that method
  never ran.

All four now ask TAOM's player query, which reads Coop's player
registry. Without a co-op session it gives the same answer as before,
so single player does not change. If the registry cannot be read, the
escape roll, the rally and the AI claims stop for everyone, and
fertility uses the AI rules.

The Realms offices pass and the grants to children still treat a
guest as AI on purpose: a guest cannot appoint officers or grant
titles, because no Realms player action reaches the host. The Refuge peace
release and the castle recruit log were checked and match vanilla
under Coop. Still open on #1141: the volunteer rate multiplier
reaches a guest's fiefs. The other models that may hide a Coop fix
the same way are #1151.

Not-tested: no co-op session has been played. Unit tests cover the
new player checks; the call sites that use them are not unit-tested.
Review: tier 1 deep review (Data flow and Engine compatibility
lenses), two MEDIUM and nine LOW findings fixed or documented; RCA
docs/reviews/rca-coop-mainhero-audit-2026-11-13.md. Codex did not
run (out of usage).

#### fix(long-defeat): v2.0.38 - Release the split at attackers at the walls

`56c2970f`

The Long Defeat's opening split now holds the defenders at their places
until the first attackers reach the walls, not until the wave spawns.

The first build took contact as a siege lane's defense level rising.
The engine raises that level as soon as an attacker formation takes one
of the lane's engines, so in the first game run both waves released the
split within a second of their start, and the gate group was still 55 m
to 64 m from the gate. The split now reads the siege AI's own count of
attackers close to each side's defender origin or on an inside navmesh
face (SiegeQuerySystem's close attacker counts). A fresh split drops the
engine's 5 s cache of those counts before it reads them, because at a
clear the cache can still hold the last wave's counts.

In the second game run (Helm's Deep, two waves) both split checks
passed: contact came 219 s into the wave 1 hold and 47 s into wave 2,
the gate group stood 2.8 m and 2.6 m from its place, and no group was
kept on a player order. The cache refresh came from the review after
that run and has unit tests only. The run itself failed on two older
defects: a soldier off the navmesh at the garrison muster (#1142) and
a field-care buy the check cannot judge (#1143).

The log and check detail now say "close" for these counts. The feature
doc, RCA rows 14 to 24 and a lesson about reading an engine state's
setter record the cause. The doc also records the multiplayer research
and BannerlordCoop's license since 2026-06-17.

#### fix(coop): v2.0.38 - Let Coop capture a defeated Sauron or Nazgul

`217540ff`

In a BannerlordCoop session two players can fight each other in a
field battle, and the loser is taken prisoner by Coop's server
(#1139). For a player who plays Sauron or one of the Nine, TAOM got in
the way: Uncapturable Heroes treated only Hero.MainHero as the player,
and on the Coop server that is the server's own hero. The defeated
player was made a fugitive instead, his party could be destroyed, and
Coop's captivity flow ran only half. The same happened when the AI
beat him.

Both Uncapturable Heroes seams now ask TAOM's player query, which
reads Coop's own player registry, and leave any player's hero to
vanilla and Coop. Without a co-op session the answer is the same as
before, so single player does not change. If the registry cannot be
read, the seams defer for every hero, so in that session no lore hero
is protected.

docs/features/coop-interop.md gains a section on battles between
players: the capture, who can fight (any two players in different
factions; Coop sets the war stance itself, #1140), and the fear
effects that reach only one side. Follow-up audit of the other
Hero.MainHero comparisons: #1141.

Not-tested: no co-op battle between players has been played. The
in-game checks are on #1139.

#### fix(coop): v2.0.38 - Skip the initial alliances on a co-op client

`a83f45ae`

A player joining a co-op game for the first time builds a local
campaign for character creation before the host's save arrives. TAOM
set up its 38 permanent alliances in that campaign too. On a client,
Coop turns each alliance into a request to the host, and each one
failed at Coop's kingdom lookup: 38 errors in Coop_client.log and 38
TAOM warnings on every first join. The host's save already holds the
alliances, so a co-op client now skips this step.

The gate reads IsCoopClient. ShouldDeferToHost, which the load-time
alliance repair uses, is also true in a solo game when TAOM cannot
probe the co-op mod, and a new campaign there would have lost its
alliances.

Tested in game with CoopMcpServer (one host and one client, then two
clients): before the fix, 38 kingdom errors on the client; after it,
the client logs the skip and none, and the host still reports 38
alliances. The deep review (data flow and engine lenses) found the
predicate issue and two wording items; the RCA is
docs/reviews/rca-coop-client-initial-alliances-2026-11-12.md.

#### fix(dependencies): v2.0.38 - PatchShield skips finalizer-only owners

`b7b6b4be`

When PatchShield strips the patches on a method after a missing-API
exception, it removes each foreign owner's prefixes, postfixes and
transpilers there, never its finalizers. An owner whose only patch on
that method was a finalizer was still logged in diag.log as unpatched
and counted in the owner totals, and the method itself was counted in
the session summary's "unpatched N target(s)" even when nothing was
stripped there (a finalizer-only or fully protected method). No patch
was removed or kept wrongly; only the log was off.

The owners the strip acts on are now chosen by
PatchShieldPolicy.OwnersToStrip from prefixes, postfixes and
transpilers only, so a finalizer-only owner is neither logged nor
counted. A method counts as unpatched (or withheld under co-op) only
once an owner there was actually stripped (or withheld); a separate
set keeps the once-per-method check.

Tests: three PatchShieldPolicy cases (no strippable owner, mixed
owners counted once, blank owners dropped).

Not-tested: the strip and the summary count (static and Harmony-bound,
no unit seam)
Refs #726.

#### fix(lordspawnguard): v2.0.38 - Guard SpawnCaravan null template

`76355bd6`

Vanilla CaravansCampaignBehavior.SpawnCaravan reads the caravan
template its predicate pick returns without a null check. The pick
returns null when nothing matches, so a culture whose caravan templates
are all land templates crashes the daily hero tick with a
NullReferenceException while its merchant is in a port town. An empty
list or a merchant with no current settlement does the same.

Patch147_CaravanTemplateGuard flags such a call in its prefix (rule in
CaravanTemplateGuard) and its finalizer contains only a
NullReferenceException on a flagged call. The template is read before
the party is created, so the merchant just sends no caravan that day
and one warning per culture names the gap. Closes #482.

Not-tested: in game; no player has hit this yet.
Save-compat: no saved state added.

#### fix(combat): v2.0.38 - charge knockdown defers on a bad health or damage

`bef8df08`

A horse charge whose victim reported a NaN or infinite maximum health,
or a hit with NaN or infinite inflicted damage, got a definite answer
from TAOM's charge rule instead of being handed back to the game's own
rule, which is what every other unreadable input already does. Such a
value turns the comparison into an answer computed from garbage.

The weight-scaled check now returns no opinion when either value is
not a finite number, and the game decides as it would without TAOM.
The overwhelming mass rule reads neither value and is unchanged.
Whether the engine can ever report such a health is unverified, so
this may not be reachable.

Tests: ChargeKnockdownService cases for a NaN and an infinite maximum
health and inflicted damage, beside the existing NaN velocity and
resistance ones.

Not-tested: in-game (no known way to produce the input)

#### fix(momentum): v2.0.38 - count a raid only when the village is looted

`e7b8ee86`

War of the Ring momentum counted a resisted village raid twice. The
game ends a raid that meets the village militia as two raid events:
one when the militia is beaten and one when the looting finishes, and
both report the raider as the winner. Each one added a raid to the
faction's totals and a raid momentum event. A raid whose looting was
interrupted after the militia fight counted a raid that never happened.

A raid now counts only when the game has marked the village as looted,
which it does just before it reports the finished raid. One resisted
raid adds one raid and one momentum event; beating the militia alone
adds nothing.

Tests: two new MomentumEventService cases (militia only, militia then
loot) and the existing raid cases now carry the looted flag, so each
guard is tested on its own.

only at zero hit points, then RaidCompleted with the winner side)

#### fix(hero-race): v2.0.38 - Repair the two wreckage death action indexes

`7e04862c`

At startup the game repairs ActionIndexCache's action indexes, which the
engine can bake to -1. Two fields, act_wreckage_death_01 and _02, are
built by the engine from other action names
(act_cutscene_main_hero_battle_death_01 and _02). The repair looked them
up by field name, found nothing and left both at -1, and every launch
logged "2 unknown to this engine build". The engine reads these two
fields for the corpse poses on battle wreckage on the campaign map.

KnownNameOverrides now maps both fields. A new test reads the installed
engine's static constructor and fails when any field name and its
action literal disagree with the map, so an engine update that adds a
divergence fails a test instead of passing unseen. Both fields exist
since v1.5.3 at the latest.

Found in the 2026-11-12 launch log. /deep-review ran at tier 1 (data
flow and engine compatibility) and found no CRITICAL or HIGH defect;
the RCA is docs/reviews/rca-action-index-cache-overrides-2026-11-12.md.
The full C# suite gave 39,025 passed and 3 failed outside this change
(an entry point over its line limit and two translation text gates).

In-game check owed: the next campaign launch should log REPAIRED 219 of

#### fix(siege): v2.0.38 - Defenders loot the fallen after a siege retreat

`ac55acb9`

When the attackers retreat from a siege assault, vanilla pays the
defender gold, renown, influence and morale but never runs its loot
step, so the gear of the attackers who fell was lost (#1121).

Patch146 is a prefix and postfix on
SiegeAssaultEventComponent.OnPlayerEncounterContinueBattle. When the
map event stands at a defender victory, the prefix runs vanilla's own
casualty-loot step and the postfix opens the inventory loot screen.
Only that step runs: the item and prisoner steps would strip besiegers
who survive and keep the siege, and vanilla captures no one from a
retreating side. A co-op client skips the loot.

Known limitation: not yet seen in a game. The in-game check is owed
(#1121, label triage-needs-ingame). Review record:
docs/reviews/rca-siege-retreat-loot-2026-11-12.md.

A town or castle owned by the buyer or their clan can be claimed even

(rgl_log_<number>.txt), which shows whether the engine was still

Also: removed BattleLoadLoadingWindow.OpenedAtUtc (only the watchdog
read it), fixed comments and docs that still described the watchdog,

#### fix(diagnostics): v2.0.38 - Remove the battle-load stall watchdog

`045e7bc4`

A slow battle load on a cold shader cache no longer produces a crash
report. Players read that report as a crash, when the game was only
compiling shaders.

Until now a background timer wrote "WATCHDOG STILL LOADING" and a crash
ZIP when a mission load stayed open for 300 seconds. On a cold shader
cache the engine compiles shaders before the first tick. One player log
held 1,388 shader compiles in those 300 seconds, and the load was still
working. The watchdog is gone.

Still there: the [BattleLoad] phase log, the once-a-second
WaitingForRender lines, the notice on the next launch after a load that
never finished, and the freeze sampler for a battle that freezes after
the load.

Also removed:
- the three Stall Watchdog options on the Battle Load Diagnostics MCM
  page (EnableStallWatchdog, EnableStallWatchdogBundle,
  StallWatchdogSeconds); saved copies of those keys are ignored
- BattleLoadRenderWaitProbe, BattleLoadStallException and the flag the
  shader precompile walk set to quiet the watchdog
- IBattleLoadDiagnosticsService.CurrentStatusLine and the unused
  BattleLoadPhase.StallWatchdog
- the stallWatchdog and stallBundle tokens in the [PerfContext] diag
  list; the Python triage and perf tools still read old logs

Known limitation: a load that never finishes now writes no crash ZIP and
no ERROR line. The phase log still names the last phase reached.

No issue filed yet; the maintainer asked for this change directly.

#### fix(mission-start-guard): v2.0.38 - Queue behavior adds during the walk

`6f32888f`

A mod that adds a mission behavior while Mission.AfterStart walks
MissionBehaviors makes the engine throw "Collection was modified" and
load the mission again (#1028). DualWield does this from its
Mission.SpawnAgent postfix. An arena practice fight started from a town
menu spawns its fighters from an AfterMissionStarted listener inside the
walk, so the first spawn adds DualWield's behavior, the mission reloads,
and the first tick of the reload throws in FocusTick. The fight started
from the arena master's dialogue spawns after the walk and was fine.
Player bundle: taom_crash_20261112_161559_ca0697d0.

The EarlyStart and AfterStart helpers of Patch103 now open a
thread-static window around their call. A bool prefix on
Mission.AddMissionBehavior queues an add made inside it, and Patch103's
AfterStart finalizer applies the queue through the engine's own method,
after a normal end and after a throw. Adds in OnBehaviorInitialize and
OnMissionBehaviorInitialize are untouched. The Survive Mission Start
Failures switch gates it, and one INFO line names each queued add.

Known limitation: a queued behavior has no Mission and has not run
OnCreated until the flush, and it misses this start's calls. DualWield
does not register the first batch of agents spawned in that gap. A
remove or a direct list change inside the walk still reloads the
mission. The limits are in docs/features/mission-start-guard.md.

Reviewed with /deep-review at tier 1 (data flow and engine
compatibility lenses): no CRITICAL or HIGH, two doc errors and four LOW
items fixed, RCA in docs/reviews/rca-mission-start-defer-2026-11-12.md.

is owed before merge. Not checked in game: start a practice fight from

#### fix(war-pledge): v2.0.38 - Count a same-day pledge in the war's outcome

`e210d7fc`

War Pledge lets a Neutral realm take a side in the middle of the War
of the Ring. The war meter keeps each side's kingdoms in a list that
it refreshed once a day. When a kingdom was destroyed, the victory
check counted that list as it stood. A realm that had joined a side
since the last refresh was not counted, so the other side could win
the war by elimination while that realm lived, and the realm was left
out of the peace that ends the war.

For players: with momentum victory on (it is off by default), a side
no longer loses the war while a realm that joined it that day is
alive, and that realm is part of the peace when the war is won. Today
only the console command taom.add_war_pledge joins a realm between
two daily refreshes; the AI's join runs before that day's refresh.
Nothing changes for a campaign with victory off.

Limits: a battle, siege, raid or army gathering of a realm that the
console pledged scores no momentum before the next daily refresh, and
the refresh does not make that good.

How: MomentumEnrollmentService.RemoveKingdom refreshes the lists after
it removes the destroyed kingdom, before the handler checks victory.
The engine marks a kingdom eliminated before it raises
KingdomDestroyed (v1.5.7 DestroyKingdomAction), so the refresh cannot
enroll that kingdom again.

Tools: analyze_war_ledger.py listed a pledge that a load of a save
from the same day had taken back. It now judges a pledge by the last
kingdom line read after it, and a later load of a save that holds the
pledge lists it again.

Tests: one test for each of eleven decisions that no test would have
caught (the daily subscription, the save keys, a war that is already
declared and others).

of vanilla Sturgian and Vlandian lords. Only that six-bit field (bits
48-53 of the key's first part) changes. Built on the folded lord
definitions, so each hero's face is changed where the game reads it
(lords.xml or the lords.xslt rebuild).
